data.name: The Buried Cache
data.description:
The chart is spent when the run starts. Health and chakra carry from fight to fight, and a lost fight ends the run.

Before the Skyglass war-ship vanished into the sky, its crew buried a field cache on this shore. The Wayfinder corrected the route to it again and again as the coast changed. This chart carries his last correction. Lose a fight and the tide takes the dig, chart and all.
data.successDescription: You dug up the Skyglass crew's field cache.

objectives.description: The chart's route ends on a quiet stretch of coast, within sight of the wreck. Among the ship's impossible routes it marks an old field cache, buried before the ship vanished. The ink is decades old. The Wayfinder's newest corrections are not.

nextObjectiveId.text: Compare the old and new routes

objectives.description: Under the first route lies a map of places that did not yet exist when the ship vanished. The Wayfinder corrected the same journey again and again as villages moved, roads changed, and generations passed. The cache is real, but the final clue must be read against the newest chart.
A notation along the route sheet reads: 'Where the cliff drinks and the stone keeps watch, the cache sleeps beneath the watcher's shadow.' Three coves match part of the description.

objectives.description: You dig where the split cliff breaks the tide. Beneath the sand you find old seal fragments, and the fragments wake: a Deck Warden pulls itself out of the sand with a seal charge still burning in its hook.
The open beach yields an abandoned anchor brace and reef stone, and something under it. A Deck Warden rises from the wet sand, dragging a seal charge with it.

data.name: The Drowned Foundry
data.description:
The chart is spent when the run starts. Health and chakra carry from fight to fight, and a lost fight ends the run.
There is no turning back: the only way out is through the crucible.

Under the wreck's keel are the works where the Core grows the skyglass that mends the hull. The sea came in when the ship came down, and the works never stopped. The water rises the deeper you go, and the haul is at the bottom: there is no way out but through the crucible. Lose a fight and the flood throws you out, chart and all.
data.successDescription: You carried the last pour out of the keel works.

objectives.description: Outside, the ship is a wreck on the sand. Inside, the Core still holds every deck the way it was. Beneath them, seal channels feed a hatch rimmed with cooled skyglass. Seawater pours past it into the dark. Somewhere below, something is still being poured.

nextObjectiveId.text: Climb down into the keel works

objectives.description: The intake is half flooded. A Deck Warden stands knee-deep in it, counting canisters that bob against the walls. Above his cloth mask his eyes are young; his gear is generations out of date. He loses count, and starts again. 'No one is relieved,' he says, as if reading it from a list.
The Deck Warden and a Core Canister hold the intake.
objectives.drawDescription: The fight stalls and the moment is lost.
objectives.fleeDescription: You break away, and the way back closes behind you.

objectives.description:
The Deck Warden sinks into the water, still counting.

Cooling racks line the first hall, stacked with fresh skyglass no one has come to collect in years. The water is at your ankles and still rising, and the hatch above has sealed behind you. A stair goes down into the pour halls.

nextObjectiveId.text: Go deeper into the pour halls

objectives.description: In the pour hall the Arsenal Keeper is checking a ledger he has checked every day for decades, beside seal charges bound to every mould. Rice that rotted a generation ago is still listed as fresh stores, and every page carries the same request for shore leave, crossed out: crew not relieved. He looks up. 'You are not in the ledger.'
The Arsenal Keeper sets off his charges.
objectives.drawDescription: The fight stalls and the moment is lost.
objectives.fleeDescription: You break away, and the way back closes behind you.

objectives.description:
"Unlisted," the Keeper says as he falls, and makes a note of it.

The water is at your knees. The pour hall's best work sits cooling on the moulds, and below it the crucible glows through the floor grates. Whatever keeps the works running is down there.

The crucible chamber is the only dry room in the works, kept dry by heat. The Foundry Warden stands in it, half fused with the pouring frame, a master smelter whose impression never set down his forge maul. 'The last pour is not finished,' he says. 'It is never finished.'
The Foundry Warden tips the crucible.
objectives.drawDescription: The fight stalls and the moment is lost.
objectives.fleeDescription: You break away, and the way back closes behind you.

objectives.description: "Finished," the Warden says, as if he does not believe it, and cools into a shell of skyglass. The last pour sits unclaimed in its mould, and the works fall silent for the first time since the ship was built.

nextObjectiveId.text: Take the last pour and leave

objectives.description: You carry the last pour out of the keel works. Behind you, the wreck is already starting to mend what you broke.
The flood takes you. You wash up on the shore below the wreck, and the chart is gone.

data.name: The Quarantined Archive
data.description:
The chart is spent when the run starts. Health and chakra carry from fight to fight, and a lost fight ends the run.
A wrong answer at a seal costs you an extra fight and a smaller haul.

This chart shows a room no other plan of the wreck admits to: an archive someone aboard sealed shut, and filed behind three seals. A wrong answer at any seal rings the alarm, and the archive's guard comes for you before you can go on. Answer all three cleanly for the better haul.
data.successDescription: The archive's last seal is broken and its records are yours.

objectives.description: The seal channels along the keel still glow, carrying the Core's chakra up into the hull. One thin line runs the wrong way, against their flow, and it carries scraps of handwriting with it, toward a part of the ship no plan admits to. Someone aboard once cut something off from the rest of the ship, and hid it.

nextObjectiveId.text: Follow the breach into the hull

objectives.description: Below the tide line the hull is mending itself out of timber and rope that do not belong together. Something large is being mended with them. The Core has lost the shape of whoever it was, and it is filling the gaps with whatever it can reach.

nextObjectiveId.text: Face what the hull is building

objectives.description: The Core Horror comes apart, and the frame around it is already sketching it back together. Beneath the ladder the wrong-way seal line runs on, toward a door with no handle.

Rows of empty recall frames stand in the dark. Each still holds an impression, not a body: a remembered greeting, a hand reaching for a cup of warm tea, an order repeated until its meaning wore away. Behind them, a small seal plate guards the way on.
You choose: Force the Captain's command seal. The seal flares red and the archive's alarm begins to toll.
You choose: Force the deck seals. The seal flares red and the archive's alarm begins to toll.

First seal. Three seal paths cross the plate. One climbs to the deck seals, one bears the Captain's command mark, and a third turns back beneath the empty frames. Beside the third someone has scratched: 'What command will not mend must first be sealed away.'

objectives.description: The last seal opens on a narrow room no plan of the ship admits to. Orders, reports and damaged crew impressions were carried down here and filed away, out of command's sight. Their keeper has not yet shown himself.

The alarm dies as you cross into the archive, too late to matter. Orders, reports and damaged crew impressions were filed away down here, out of command's sight. Their keeper already knows you are coming.

The reports span decades, all in one seal-smith's hand. Each warns that the crew's impressions are fraying: names forgotten, faces filled in wrong, men coming back as less each time. Each asks leave to let them rest. Every answer is the same, sealed in cyan wax under a crown of jagged frost points around one tall central blade, sent down from a fortress called Crownhold: 'Refused. None is relieved.'

An old seal-smith gathers out of the engraved lines, steadier than the broken crew below. A black iron reliquary is chained to the wall behind him. 'I sealed away what I could not mend,' the Sealwright says. 'The crown would not let me stop the work. It will not let you take these records either.' He raises a sealing stance, and he does not look as though he wants to.
The Sealwright is waiting, already in his sealing stance. 'You came through my alarms,' he says. 'Then you have seen enough to know what this place is for.'
The Sealwright steps back into the reliquary's light, and does not leave it.

data.name: The Captain's Watch
data.description:
The chart is spent when the run starts. Health and chakra carry from fight to fight, and a lost fight ends the run.
Every term you accept makes a fight harder and the haul bigger.

The Captain still keeps the night watch on his broken command deck, and he never refuses a challenger. But the Oathkeeper sets terms: before each fight you may accept a handicap. Every term you take and survive raises the haul. Lose any fight and the watch is over.
data.successDescription: You kept the Captain's watch and claimed its stores.

objectives.description: The chart's route ends at a cove below the wreck, where the ship's boat is drawn up on the sand, waiting. The Oathkeeper stands beside it, in an officer's coat faded by no weather. 'The Captain keeps the night watch,' he says. 'He will meet you. I set the terms. We have time for terms. We have always had time.'

In the chart room the Wayfinder looks up from decades of corrections to a coastline that keeps moving. 'Still no home port,' he says. The Oathkeeper speaks from the doorway: 'Fight him without your elements, and the Captain will hear of it.'
You refuse the term. The Wayfinder redraws the room around you.
Your elements go quiet. The Wayfinder waits.

He glances back at the empty ring and touches his bare head above the white mask, as if something should sit there. 'I keep his watch,' he says, to no one. 'I wear his mask.
